examples.en: It's cold outside, so I wear a hat.
My eyesight is bad, so I go around wearing glasses.
It's a little hard to breathe when I wear a mask.
The sun is strong today, so wear sunglasses.

examples.ko: 자전거를 탈 때는 헬멧을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when riding a bike.

examples.ko: 어제 제가 쓴 모자 못 봤어요?
examples.en: Did you see the hat I wore yesterday?

explain: 모자, 안경, 마스크, 선글라스처럼 머리나 얼굴에 올리는 것에 써요. 옷은 '입다', 신발은 '신다', 시계는 '차다', 반지는 '끼다'를 써요. 우산을 쓰다(use an umbrella)도 같은 '쓰다'예요. 벗을 때는 '벗다'를 써요.

phrases.en: My eyesight is bad, so I wear glasses.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for putting on or wearing glasses.

explain_en: Use it for things you put on your head or face, such as hats, glasses, masks and sunglasses. Clothes use '입다', shoes use '신다', watches use '차다' and rings use '끼다'. Putting up an umbrella is also '쓰다', and taking things off is '벗다'.

t90.ax: It's cold outside, so I wear a hat.

examples.en: This coffee is too bitter. Do you have sugar?

examples.ko: 이 약은 입에 쓰지만 꼭 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine tastes bitter, but you must take it.
If you don't add sugar, it tastes bitter.

examples.ko: 너무 쓰면 우유를 조금 넣어 보세요.
examples.en: If it's too bitter, try adding a little milk.
My mouth tastes bitter, so I can't eat.

examples.ko: 이 채소는 맛이 좀 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This vegetable can taste a bit bitter.

explain: 맛을 말하는 '쓰다'는 형용사라서 '써요, 써서'처럼 '아/어' 앞에서 '으'가 빠지고, 꾸밀 때는 '쓴 커피'가 돼요. 반대말은 '달다'예요. 글을 쓰다·모자를 쓰다는 동사라서 '쓰는 사람'처럼 '는'이 붙어요.

phrases.en: I got a bitter taste of failure when my first business failed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실패나 어려움을 직접 겪고 힘들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means going through failure or hardship yourself and finding it painful.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a taste of hardship

explain_en: As a taste word it is an adjective. The '으' drops before '아/어', as in 써요 and 써서, and it becomes '쓴 커피' when modifying a noun. Its opposite is '달다' (sweet). The verbs for writing and wearing take '는', as in '쓰는 사람'.

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 값을 조금 깎아 줬어요.
examples.en: The shop owner gave me a small discount.

explain: '깎다'는 여기서 값을 낮추는 것이에요. 시장에서 '좀 깎아 주세요'라고 해요. 사과를 깎다(peel)와는 다른 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: I want to bargain the price down.

explain_en: 깎다 here means lowering a price. In a market you say 좀 깎아 주세요. It differs from peeling an apple.

examples.en: I ran three laps around the playground.

explain: '바퀴'는 여기서 어떤 곳을 한 번 도는 횟수를 세는 말이에요. '한 바퀴, 두 바퀴'로 세요. 자동차 바퀴(wheel)와 달라요.

phrases.en: I walk one lap around the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아서 처음 자리로 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you come back to the start.

phrases.en: I went one lap around the playground.

explain_en: 바퀴 here counts how many times you go around a place: 한 바퀴, 두 바퀴. It differs from a car wheel.

explain: '붓다'는 몸의 한 곳이 부풀어 오르는 것이에요. '다리가 붓다', '얼굴이 붓다'로 써요. 'ㅅ 불규칙'이라서 '부어요', '부었어요'가 돼요. 물을 붓다(pour)와 달라요.

phrases.en: My face swells when I eat ramen.
phrases.nuance_en: The body part is the subject.

explain_en: Body part swelling from injury or illness (다리가 붓다) 붓다 here means a body part swelling. You say 다리가 붓다 and 얼굴이 붓다. It is ㅅ-irregular, so it becomes 부어요 and 부었어요. It differs from pouring water.

explain: '깎다'는 칼 같은 도구로 겉을 얇게 벗기거나 자르는 것이에요. '사과를 깎다', '연필을 깎다'처럼 써요. 값을 낮추는 '깎다'는 다른 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: I got my hair cut at the hair salon.
phrases.nuance_en: You also use 깎다 for cutting hair short.

phrases.en: I cut my nails on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_en: For nails, people say 깎다 more often than 자르다.

explain_en: 깎다 here means peeling or trimming the surface with a tool like a knife: 사과를 깎다, 연필을 깎다. Bargaining a price down is a different meaning.
